html:
Melchior Ndadaye was the first democratically elected president of Burundi and its first Hutu head of state, in office for just over three months in 1993.

A teacher and banker, he fled to Rwanda as a young man after the Ikiza of 1972. He led the party Frodebu to victory in Burundi's first free elections in June 1993, defeating the Tutsi military president Pierre Buyoya, who accepted the result.

On 21 October 1993 Tutsi soldiers killed him in a coup attempt. Hutu across the country rose and killed Tutsi, and the army answered by killing Hutu. Tens of thousands died within weeks, beginning the civil war. The news reached Rwanda months before its own genocide.
